title: QUIC RFC 9000 STREAM Frame Focused Proof
purpose: Describe the focused proof boundary for RFC 9000 STREAM frame encoding, parsing, and receive-state policy requirements.
design_summary: The STREAM frame proof is decomposed into requirement-home tests over the existing STREAM parser, formatter, frame-bit constants, and receive-side stream-state policy. Parser proof covers OFF, LEN, and FIN bits, type values 0x08 through 0x0f, Stream ID, Offset, Length, Stream Data consumption, varint truncation, zero-length boundaries, and the maximum stream offset ceiling. Runtime proof covers the current connection-stream-state policy that rejects uncreated local streams and local send-only streams with STREAM_STATE_ERROR while accepting a peer-created bidirectional receive stream, plus receive-credit excess classification as FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.
data_and_state_considerations: The slice primarily adds focused proof over existing parser and stream-state behavior. The helper constructs exact STREAM frame byte sequences, including deliberately mismatched declared lengths, so individual requirement homes do not depend on broad parser tests.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Explicit zero offsets remain distinguishable from absent offsets when the OFF bit is set.
Zero-length STREAM frames are accepted when LEN is set and consume no stream data.
LEN-clear STREAM frames consume every remaining byte in the packet payload slice.
The largest legal stream offset is accepted only when no delivered data would exceed the varint maximum.
Malformed, truncated, non-STREAM, and over-ceiling frame encodings are rejected by the parser before receive-state mutation.
alternatives_considered: Keep broad stream parser tests as the only evidence; rejected because generated triage requires direct requirement-home proof.
Introduce a separate STREAM parser facade; rejected because the existing parser and formatter already own the wire encoding behavior.
Broaden the slice into every S19 frame type; rejected because S19 still contains several independent frame families that need separate bounded proof.
risks: The parser reports malformed STREAM encodings as parse failure, while exact close-datagram emission remains owned by packet-processing requirements.
The slice does not claim public API stream behavior or application protocol semantics beyond the receive-state policy tested here.
Other S19 frame families remain non-clean and are not closed by this proof.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design covers focused S19P8 STREAM frame proof only: parser/formatter encoding behavior, maximum-offset guard, and current receive-state error policy for invalid STREAM frame targets.
